fatal_errors: The proposed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy is not the studied AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA and lacks the target L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The proposed 500–700 °C saline-solution regime is incompatible with the target aqueous tests at 25–100 °C and is physically underdefined without a pressurized or molten-salt apparatus.
The hypothesis omits the rapid 1100 °C thermal-shock comparison and the demonstrated phase stability relative to duplex stainless steel 2205.
The cited evidence does not demonstrate elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion performance of CoCrFeMnNi or validate the proposed test conditions.
High configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion are asserted as the operative mechanism without evidence connecting them to tribofilm stability under sliding.
explanation: The response addresses the broad idea that an HEA might outperform a conventional alloy through passivation, but it reconstructs neither the material nor the experimental regime. The hidden study concerns an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA tested against DS2205 in deionized water from 25 to 100 °C, with minimum degradation near 50 °C and failure of tribolayer stability at 100 °C. The generated hypothesis instead proposes the Cantor alloy in an undefined saline solution at 500–700 °C and supplies a generic entropy/sluggish-diffusion explanation. Its predicted superiority is directionally similar but misses the temperature-dependent wear minimum, phase-retention evidence, friction and wear-rate results, and specific comparator. The proposed experiment includes useful measurements, but the 600 °C saline-solution condition is not operationally credible as written, and mass loss alone would poorly separate mechanical wear from corrosion. E1 concerns protective oxides and molten-fluoride corrosion, while E2 only provides general background on CoCrFeMnNi; neither supports the claimed tribo-corrosion mechanism or performance.
